tex_content.html:
\begin{exercise} \end{exercise}1. ch2:2-2

Suppose $V$ and $W$ are finite-dimensional real inner product spaces of the same dimension, and $F: V \to W$ is any map (not assumed to be linear or even continuous) that preserves the origin and all distances: $F(0) = 0$ and $|F(x) - F(y)| = |x - y|$ for all $x, y \in V$. Prove that $F$ is a linear isometry. [Hint: First show that $F$ preserves inner products, and then show that it is linear.] (Used on p. 187.) \end{exercise}
